scope: Configuration, MCP readiness and explicit client resume only; R6/R6L/R8 remain open
candidate_source_note: Repository base commit; source snapshots and dirty inputs below identify the current harness state

working_tree_inputs.build_attestation: Source snapshot only; exact probe binaries hashed separately

implementation_commit_note: Every harness source hash in the raw report was compared with this committed source after the run.
redaction: Absolute executable, profile and log paths, native session identifiers, tool definitions, provider headers and raw client output omitted. Fixture secrets were never retained in the report. Protocol event PIDs are omitted; same-session comparisons are retained as booleans.

probe_build.qualification: Developer fixture build from the current checkout; dirty inputs are recorded above, and exact executed probe bytes are hashed below.

invocation_note: Used the four existing installed client executables, the existing ignored Pi 1.0.1 package, a 30000ms per-operation/cleanup budget, fresh disposable profiles, scripted loopback providers and the required sandbox preflight. No clients were installed, accounts authenticated or owner profiles modified.
cleanup_evidence_note: Natural cleanup means exit without harness TERM/KILL within the authored grace period, restricted to the owned process session and receipt-identified bridges. It does not establish immediate cancellation or containment of unobserved fully detached descendants.

clients.interruption_interpretation: The harness predicate passed with no forced cleanup, but lifecycle elapsed 30391ms against a 30000ms fixture I/O budget and the bridge recorded the held wait completing with success=false. This is consistent with exit after the fixture I/O timeout; immediate cancellation of the bridge by Pi was not established.
